SkyTruth Analysis

Report Description
CALLER IS REPORTING THAT WHILE RETURNING ON HIS SEA RAY 370 AN EXPLOSION OCCURRED IN THE ENGINE COMPARTMENT AND SMOKE BILLOWED OUT OF THE ENGINE BAY. CALLER CAME TO IDLE AND SHUT DOWN THE ENGINES. CALLER THEN CALLED MAYDAY ON RADIO FOR COAST GUARD REGARDING A FIRE ON THE VESSEL. ANCHORS COULD NOT BE LOOSEN DUE TO POWER SHUT DOWN. A GOOD SAMARITAN TOOK CAPTAIN OF THE VESSEL AND PASSENGERS OFF THE BOAT. THE VESSEL CAUGHT ON FIRE THROUGH THE ENGINE COMPARTMENT AND BURNED FOR ABOUT AN HOUR AND SANK. ON SATURDAY 14TH APRIL A SALVAGE COMPANY RECOVERED THE VESSEL. NO SHEEN WAS REPORTED OR NOTICED ON THE WATER.

Report Description
***48 HOUR PHMSA UPDATE FOR REPORT 1198866*** ORIGINAL REPORT: **UPDATE TO A PREVIOUS NRC REPORT** THE RP IS REPORTING A RELEASE OF NATURAL GAS DUE TO A THIRD PARTY STRIKING AN UNDERGROUND PIPELINE. THE INCIDENT INVOLVES A FARMING TILING MACHINE. RP REPORTS THERE WAS AN IGNITION DUE TO THE STRIKE AND THE LOCAL FD REPORTS THAT THERE WERE TWO (2) INJURIES AND TWO (2) REPORTED FATALITIES. RP STATED THE TWO INJURED INDIVIDUALS WERE TRANSPORTED TO A LOCAL HOSPITAL. RP STATED THAT THE LOCAL FIRE CHIEF CONFIRMED THE TWO FATALITIES. NO REPORTED EVACUATIONS. THE AREA WAS SECURED AND ROADS WERE CLOSED. THE AMOUNT RELEASED IS BELIEVED TO EXCEED THE 3000 MCF. DAMAGE COST ARE CURRENTLY UNKNOWN. **THE LINE IS CLASS 1, DOT REGULATED. 20" DIAMETER, .281 WALL THICKNESS. X40 GRADE. **MAOP IS 800. OPERATING PRESSURE AT THE TIME OF THE INCIDENT WAS IN THE LOW 700S. 13.6 MILES OF PIPE WAS ISOLATED IN RESPONSE TO THE INCIDENT. **ORIGINAL NRC# 1198853** CALLER REPORTS A RELEASE OF AN UNKNOWN AMOUNT OF NATURAL GAS INTO AIR CAUSED BY AN UNKNOWN REASON FROM A PIPELINE. ***UPDATED INFORMATION: UPDATES TO RELEASE VOLUME AND REPAIR COST.
